target_customer: ASMR fans, many who use it to sleep, plus ASMR creators who earn through subscriptions
problem: ASMR viewers got interrupted by YouTube ads while trying to relax or sleep, and creators had weak ways to be paid.
business_model: Ad free video app funded by viewer subscriptions and creator tips
product_category: ASMR video streaming app for relaxation and sleep

founders.name: Miha Mlakar
founders.background_notes: Slovenian per TechCrunch 2018-03-16; YC profile lists Popsy S22.

exit.reason: YC lists inactive, but gettingles.com still shows a Tingles app with a 2024 copyright and 1,500 creators. A second app of the same name by another developer also exists.

competitors.name: YouTube
competitors.what: Main host of ASMR videos; great for discovery but ads disrupt sleep
competitors.traction_then: Main source of ASMR content; Tingles reported about 60,000 monthly users

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile video app with subscriptions and creator tools, standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Creators could move back to YouTube, though exclusive creator relationships were an edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: YouTube remained the main ASMR home; no sign that it copied the ad free model in the sources opened.

market_need_then: ASMR was described as fast growing, and Tingles had about 60,000 monthly active users and more than 200 creators by March 2018 with little promotion.

branding.name_origin: A co-creator said on Product Hunt that the name comes from the ASMR community, where people describe the sensation as feeling tingles.
branding.domain_note: Uses gettingles.com, a get prefix domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Calming, creator friendly, ad free promise

branding.brand_signature: Ad free ASMR with one tap support for artists
branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt on 2018-03-19 and covered by TechCrunch; a separate Tingles ASMR app by another developer reuses the name.

brand_strength.rationale: Instantly understandable to ASMR fans and got press and a Product Hunt launch, but name collisions diluted it.

outcome_analysis: Tingles built an ad free ASMR video app with 60,000 monthly users and 200 creators in March 2018, and joined YC in winter 2018. Databases show a small convertible note and seed worth about $120K to $125K. YC lists the company inactive while its website still promotes the app in 2024, so the outcome is unclear and the cause is not public.
notes: Funding rests only on aggregators. CB Insights gives $120K over 3 rounds with the latest a convertible note on 2018-05-31 and names the investors; Dealroom gives a $125K seed at a $2.0M valuation, which is an estimate. No press announcement found. The cause of the inactive status is not public; the website suggests the product still operates, so the status conflicts with YC. The Tingles ASMR app on app stores belongs to InitiateHub and is a different project.
